stories.title: Andy Burnham to give regional mayors share of income tax
stories.summary: PM Andy Burnham is preparing a 'No 10 North' plan to devolve fiscal powers, including a share of income tax and business rates, to regional mayors, as part of a rebalancing of power away from Whitehall.

stories.title: Burnham to free mayors from ‘Treasury death grip’ with new devolved powers
stories.summary: The PM is pushing ahead with plans to hand mayors greater fiscal autonomy, part of his wider devolution agenda since taking office.

stories.title: Burnham the crowd-pleaser knows how to make friends, but he’ll be defined by how he makes enemies
stories.summary: Comment piece assessing Burnham’s early style as PM and the challenges of turning popularity into durable political change.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤖 New AI Taskforce names Patrick Vallance as chair
stories.summary: The UK government has named Sir Patrick Vallance to chair a new AI Taskforce, signalling continued central focus on AI policy and adoption under the new administration.

stories.title: 🏢 London buys vote counting tools and plans tourist tax IT system in £17.5m tech deals
stories.summary: City Hall has signed £17.5m worth of technology contracts covering vote-counting tools and a new tourist tax IT system, among the latest public sector tech procurement activity.

stories.title: 🤖 Companies House deploys AI to help handle 300 chats a day
stories.summary: Companies House has rolled out AI tools to manage around 300 daily chat interactions and large volumes of email correspondence, part of wider public sector AI adoption.

stories.title: 🤝 Google dropped from DfE’s AI tutoring pilot, replaced by PA Consulting
stories.summary: The Department for Education has removed Google from its AI tutoring pilot programme, replacing it with UK consultancy PA Consulting — a notable vendor/consulting signal.

stories.title: 🏢 MoD awards BAE AI, software and augmented reality deal
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence has awarded BAE Systems a £708 million deal covering AI, software and augmented reality to accelerate next-generation air combat technology development.

stories.title: 💰 Post Office: Signing of Horizon replacement deal set back a further three weeks
stories.summary: The long-running Horizon IT replacement programme at the Post Office faces further delay, with the contract signing pushed back another three weeks — a public sector spending/delivery signal.

stories.title: 🤖 Judge’s AI hallucination warning on Home Office evidence
stories.summary: A tribunal judge warned that AI may have ‘hallucinated’ evidence used to refuse an asylum claim after a document central to the case was found not to exist — raising fresh questions about AI use in government decision-making.

stories.title: 📄 Research Report — Building No. 10 North (re-state.co.uk)
stories.summary: Re:State think tank paper (Dr Simon Kaye, July 2026) sets out a blueprint for Burnham’s ‘No 10 North’: (1) it must avoid being mere symbolism, too small, or business-as-usual — physical relocation alone won’t create institutional change; (2) proposes four core units — Devolution, Subnational Investment & Growth, System Democratisation, and Local Public Services Innovation — plus a Transformation Directorate; (3) draws a comparison to the Darlington Economic Campus, arguing critical mass and recruiting diverse talent are key to success; (4) warns No 10 North must not become another Whitehall silo coordinating sign-off, but should genuinely shift power to Strategic Authorities/mayors; (5) frames the mission explicitly around devolving power, resources and decisions to subnational government — directly relevant to Burnham’s reindustrialisation and devolution agenda.

stories.title: House of Commons — Hansard record, 29–30 July sittings
stories.summary: Commons proceedings continued this week with debates recorded in Hansard; BBC Parliament carried live coverage of Thursday’s sittings.

stories.title: Diane Abbott and Joani Reid readmitted as Labour MPs
stories.summary: Diane Abbott and Joani Reid have been readmitted to the Labour Party following earlier suspensions, in a move seen as part of efforts to unify the party under new PM Andy Burnham.

stories.title: MP Diane Abbott readmitted into Labour Party after suspension
stories.summary: Abbott said the party leadership "obviously" wants her out despite her reinstatement, highlighting ongoing internal tensions.

stories.title: Labour asks Electoral Commission to investigate Reform UK over donations
stories.summary: Labour has formally asked the Electoral Commission to investigate donations to Reform UK linked to George Cottrell, an ally and adviser to Nigel Farage.

stories.title: Jenrick urges Burnham to rule out tax rises to fund social care
stories.summary: Tory frontbencher Robert Jenrick has called on PM Burnham to rule out tax increases to fund social care reform, after Kemi Badenoch wrote to Burnham on the issue.

stories.title: Burnham says he told Trump UK will be pragmatic about North Sea oil
stories.summary: Burnham said he told Donald Trump the UK would take a pragmatic approach on North Sea oil, a reversal Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch had previously called for and once branded "absurd" to expect from Labour.

stories.title: Lib Dem leader Ed Davey says he’ll boycott Trump’s state visit
stories.summary: Ed Davey has said he will boycott Donald Trump’s upcoming state visit, a stance that could put pressure on other party leaders to follow suit.

stories.title: Labour asks Electoral Commission to investigate Reform UK over donations
stories.summary: Donations to Reform UK linked to George Cottrell — a close ally and adviser to Nigel Farage — are under scrutiny, with the Met also investigating related payments.

stories.title: Even GB News cringes as Reform turns dementia patients into a political football
stories.summary: Reform UK faced criticism, including from sympathetic outlets, over its handling of a social care/dementia-related political attack line.

stories.title: ‘Farage’s got to come clean or clear off’: what voters in Clacton think
stories.summary: Voters in Farage’s Clacton constituency weigh in on the ongoing donations controversy and his self-imposed by-election, ahead of the vote.

stories.title: SNP kept tax advisory group alive to avoid bad headlines
stories.summary: Members of the Scottish Government’s Tax Advisory Group privately told officials the body had no real bearing on tax decisions, raising questions about its purpose.

stories.title: Sturgeon’s book tour resumes — the SNP won’t be happy
stories.summary: Nicola Sturgeon’s paperback book tour is resuming, again drawing attention to the SNP and the ongoing Operation Branchform case.

stories.title: Senior councillor cautions against ‘anti-SNP’ Princes Street framing
stories.summary: An SNP group leader called for all parties to show "actual leadership" over ongoing Edinburgh tram disruption rather than politicising it.

stories.title: Department for Business and Trade renamed Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
stories.summary: DBT was formally renamed to the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) as of 20 July 2026, reflecting a machinery-of-government change under the new administration.

stories.title: Polls open in Greater Manchester mayoral by-election
stories.summary: Voters went to the polls today in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election, triggered by Andy Burnham’s move to No. 10; Labour’s Bev Craig was tipped for a comfortable win over Reform, with results due Friday.

stories.title: Polling gives Bev Craig a 20-point lead over Reform in Greater Manchester
stories.summary: A More in Common poll ahead of the vote gave Labour’s Bev Craig, leader of Manchester City Council, a 20-percentage-point lead over Reform UK’s Sian Astley.
